## DESTINY-Breast03 Trial: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (T-DXd) vs Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1)

**DESTINY-Breast03** is a phase III, open-label, randomized trial that enrolled **524 patients** with HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer who had previously been treated with trastuzumab and a taxane. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd, 5.4 mg/kg) or trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1, 3.6 mg/kg) every 3 weeks.

### Key Efficacy Results

- **Progression-free survival (PFS):** At the initial interim analysis, 12-month PFS was **75.8% with T-DXd vs 34.1% with T-DM1** (HR 0.28; 95% CI 0.22–0.37), representing a **72% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death**.
- **Updated PFS (Lancet 2023):** With longer follow-up, median PFS was **28.8 months with T-DXd vs 6.8 months with T-DM1**.
- **Further update (41-month follow-up, 2024):** Median PFS was **29.0 months vs 7.2 months** (HR 0.30; 95% CI 0.24–0.38).
- **Overall survival (OS):** A significant OS benefit was observed, with an HR of **0.64** in the updated analysis.
- **Objective response rate (ORR):** Confirmed ORR was **79.7% with T-DXd vs 34.2% with T-DM1**.

### Brain Metastases Subgroup

In patients with brain metastases at baseline, T-DXd also showed substantial benefit:
- Median PFS: **15.0 months (T-DXd) vs 3.0 months (T-DM1)** (HR 0.25; 95% CI 0.13–0.45)
- Systemic ORR: **67.4% vs 20.5%**
- Intracranial ORR: **65.7% vs 34.3%**

### Safety Profile

- T-DXd was associated with **higher rates of adverse events** compared to T-DM1, including more chemotherapy-like side effects (nausea, alopecia ~30%).
- **Interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis** occurred in approximately **10.5% of T-DXd patients vs 1.9% with T-DM1**, though most cases were low grade with no grade 4–5 events in the primary report.
- Drug-related treatment discontinuation rates were higher with T-DXd (**22.6% vs 7.3%** at longer follow-up).
- Patient-reported outcomes showed that T-DXd was associated with **maintained or improved quality of life** despite the higher toxicity rates.

### Clinical Impact

DESTINY-Breast03 established trastuzumab deruxtecan as the new **standard of care for second-line treatment** of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, displacing trastuzumab emtansine. The trial led to regulatory approvals in the US, EU, Japan, and other regions, and T-DXd is now a guideline-recommended treatment in this setting.
